subject.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads

question: Should approved script operands remain arbitrarily large through an asynchronous hashing path, or should approval intentionally deny operands above a documented size limit?
rationale: The patch’s bounded-memory design resolves the prior compatibility concern but not the hot-path synchronous availability risk; choosing a size ceiling instead is a behavior and compatibility policy decision.

options.title: Use asynchronous hashing
options.body: Refactor the approval snapshot and revalidation path to hash large operands asynchronously, preserving existing large-script approval behavior without monopolizing the event loop.

options.title: Adopt a size ceiling
options.body: Reject operands above a carefully chosen documented limit before hashing, with compatibility tests and clear denial behavior for existing large scripts.

recommendation.title: Use asynchronous hashing
recommendation.body: Refactor the approval snapshot and revalidation path to hash large operands asynchronously, preserving existing large-script approval behavior without monopolizing the event loop.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the competing cap and chunked-hash iterations and are best positioned to update the proposal once the approval policy is chosen.
